newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan's Arab Bank sets up Islamic bank.
newsitem.headline: Jordan's Arab Bank sets up Islamic bank.

text.p: Arab Bank said on Tuesday it had set up Jordan's second Islamic bank, Arab Islamic International Bank, with capital of 40 million dinars ($56.5 million), using the licence of a failed investment bank.

"At the request of the Central Bank to buy the troubled bank, Amman Bank for Investment, the Arab Bank has agreed to buy its license and set up the Arab Islamic International Bank," Arab Bank chairman, Abdul-Majid Shoman, told Reuters.
The new wholly-owned subsidiary of Arab Bank, one of the leading financial institutions in the region, would start its banking operations under Islamic banking rules immediately, Shoman said.
Jordan's Central Bank took control of troubled Amman Bank for Investment last March, effectively putting the loss-making bank, one of Jordan's six investment banks, under its custody.

Arab Bank, by far Jordan's largest bank with an extensive global network and total assets of over $20.7 billion, was prodded by the Central Bank to swallow up Amman Bank for Investment after various failed attempts to salvage it, bankers said.

Arab Bank won attractive terms for the sale which liquidated the bank as a legal entity and ensures it is not liable for the troubled bank's doubtful debts, estimated to be in excess of 20 million dinars.
Under the deal, the liabilities would be assumed by the Central Bank while Arab Bank would only take over whatever assets and deposits it had, Shoman said.
"There are no obligations or liabilities on Arab Bank, the Central Bank will take over the troubled bank's debts. We will get the bank clean of any liabilities," said Shoman without elaborating.

The Arab Bank, the oldest Palestinian bank established in Jerusalem in 1930, is primarily interested in using the bank's lucrative license to operate an Islamic banking unit, seen as a future growth area.
Jordan Central Bank has practically stopped issuing bank licenses in what it views as an overcrowded banking market with 20 private banks.
The new Arab Islamic International Bank will operate in Jordan and targets expansion in both the Arab world and internationally, Shoman said.
